info.title: rest-api-access-your-mixmax-data
info.description: The Mixmax REST API, optimized for lightweight, real-time interactions. This specification is the source of truth for the definition-backed API reference on developer.mixmax.com: it lives in the api repository (openapi/openapi.yaml) and is published from CI.

get.description:
**Limited beta.** The Calls read API is currently gated by an access allowlist; callers without access receive `404` responses. To request access, email [developer@mixmax.com](mailto:developer@mixmax.com).

Streams a completed call's recording as MP3 audio. Requires the Dialer `calling` feature on your workspace. Managed API keys require the `calls:read` permission. Mixmax authenticates to the telephony provider and streams the bytes back; there is no durable, shareable media URL.

`Range` requests are honored so audio players can seek (such responses are `206 Partial Content`). Responses are private to the caller and must not be cached.

This endpoint has its own rate limit of 20 requests per minute per user, in addition to the API-wide limit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call `_id`, from `GET /calls`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Pass `workspace` to fetch a workspace member's recording. Requires workspace admin access; other callers receive a `403`.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Standard HTTP byte-range header, honored for seeking (for example `bytes=0-`).

206.description: A byte range of the recording audio, when a `Range` header was sent.

403.description: Returned in three cases: `scope=workspace` was requested without workspace admin access (JSON body), a managed API key was used without the `calls:read` permission or outside the workspace it was made in (JSON body), or the workspace does not have the Dialer `calling` feature (empty body).

404.description: The call does not exist, has no recording, the recording is no longer available, or the caller does not have access to the Calls API beta.

409.description: The recording exists but cannot be retrieved (for example, it is encrypted).

429.description: Too many recording requests. Honor the `Retry-After` response header when present. The per-endpoint limiter responds with a short plain string served as `text/html`; the telephony provider's passed-through throttle responds with JSON.

502.description: The recording could not be retrieved from the telephony provider.

get.description:
**Limited beta.** The Calls read API is currently gated by an access allowlist; callers without access receive `404` responses. To request access, email [developer@mixmax.com](mailto:developer@mixmax.com).

Returns the transcript of a completed call. Requires the Dialer `calling` feature on your workspace, and transcription must be enabled for the workspace. By default you read your own calls; workspace admins can pass `scope=workspace` to read any member's. Managed API keys require the `calls:read` permission.

When transcription is complete, `turns` holds the normalized, time-ordered speaker turns. While it is still in progress or if it failed, `turns` is empty and `status` reflects the state. Responses are private to the caller and must not be cached.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call `_id`, from `GET /calls`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Pass `workspace` to read a workspace member's transcript. Requires workspace admin access; other callers receive a `403`.

200.description: The call's transcript. `turns` is populated only when `status` is `completed`; for `queued` or `failed` it is an empty array.

callId.description: The call `_id` this transcript belongs to.

turns.description: Normalized transcript turns, in spoken order. Empty until completed.

name.description: Speaker label for the turn (for example `Speaker 0`).

message.description: The spoken text of the turn.

timestamp.description: Offset of the turn from the start of the recording, in seconds.

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language detected for the transcript (for example `en-US`).

recordingSid.description: Identifier of the source recording with the telephony provider.

transcriptionId.description: Identifier of the transcription with the telephony provider.

turns.name: Speaker 0
turns.message: Hi, this is Alex from Mixmax.

404.description: The call does not exist, has no transcript, or the caller does not have access to the Calls API beta.

get.description:
**Limited beta.** The Calls read API is currently gated by an access allowlist; callers without access receive `404` responses. To request access, email [developer@mixmax.com](mailto:developer@mixmax.com).

Lists calls placed with the Mixmax Dialer, newest first. By default you see your own calls; workspace admins can pass `scope=workspace` to list calls for every current member of their workspace (for example, to feed a conversation-intelligence integration). Calls placed by users who have been removed from the workspace, or whose Mixmax account was deleted, are not returned. A later change will keep returning calls placed in the workspace after that change ships, even once their user has left.

Each call includes `user`, the name and email of the Mixmax user who placed it, so you can attribute calls without a separate lookup. If Mixmax cannot look those up, the request fails with a `503` instead of returning calls without them; retry the same request after the `Retry-After` delay.

Only calls that were actually dialed are returned. Recording audio is not included — use `GET /calls/{id}/recording` with the returned `_id` (recording playback requires the Dialer `calling` feature on your workspace).

Managed API keys require the `calls:read` permission, which also covers `GET /calls/{id}/recording` and `GET /calls/{id}/transcript`. A key reads the calls of the member it acts for, and `scope=workspace` only when that member is a workspace admin. A key works only while its member belongs to the workspace it was made in.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results per page. Values above 200 are clamped to 200.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: previous
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response to fetch the previous page.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in each result (for example `fields=_id,status,comments`). Fields outside the documented `Call` schema are ignored. `user` is returned whole: `user`, `user.name` and `user.email` each include the full `user` object.

parameters.name: hasRecording
parameters.description: Filter to calls whose recording media is available (`true`) or not (`false`). Any other value returns a `400`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Pass `workspace` to list calls for the workspace's current members. Calls placed by users who have been removed from the workspace, or whose account was deleted, are not returned. Requires workspace admin access; other callers receive a `403`.

400.description: Invalid parameter (for example a malformed `hasRecording` value).

403.description: `scope=workspace` was requested without workspace admin access, or a managed API key was used without the `calls:read` permission or outside the workspace it was made in.

404.description: The caller does not have access to the Calls API beta.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable (for example, the users who placed the calls could not be looked up). Retry the same request after Retry-After seconds; if the header is absent, back off and retry.

get.description: Lists Mixmax tasks visible to the API key owner. The endpoint supports the same task types, filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination as the Mixmax Tasks product. Regular users can read their own assigned tasks. Workspace admins can request tasks for users they are authorized to manage, including `assignee:Everyone`. Managed API keys require the `tasks:read` permission.

parameters.description: Saved-search context. Use `all` when supplying a custom task query.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Task filter and sort expression, for example `type:email assignee:Myself status:open sortBy:due sortDir:asc`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of tasks to return in one page.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: previous
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response to fetch the previous page.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: IANA timezone used when evaluating task due dates.

200.description: A page of tasks visible to the API key owner.

403.description: A managed API key was used without the `tasks:read` permission.

429.description: The caller or downstream task service exceeded its request limit.

500.description: Mixmax could not retrieve tasks from the task service.

get.description:
Search and retrieve meeting summaries with optional filters. Returns summaries for meetings where the authenticated user is the owner, or if workspace-wide access is enabled via admin settings, summaries for all workspace members.

**Required Feature:** `mixmaxApi` (API access must be enabled for your workspace)

**Workspace Access:** If "Allow workspace-wide transcript access via API" is enabled in Admin Settings > Meeting Copilot, users can access summaries from all workspace members' meetings.

parameters.name: isExternal
parameters.description: Filter for external meetings (meetings with attendees outside your organization). Set to `true` for external meetings only, `false` for internal meetings only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start date for the search range. Only meetings on or after this date will be returned. ISO 8601 format.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End date for the search range. Only meetings on or before this date will be returned. ISO 8601 format.

parameters.name: attendee
parameters.description: Filter by attendee email address. Returns meetings where this email was an attendee.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Search by meeting title. Performs a case-insensitive partial match.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of results to skip for pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description:
Filter by meeting ownership. Accepted values:
- `me` - Returns only meetings owned by the authenticated user.
- `shared` - Returns only meetings that have been shared with the authenticated user.
- `workspace` - Returns all meetings from the workspace. Requires the authenticated user to be a workspace admin with "Allow workspace-wide transcript access via API" enabled in Admin Settings Meeting Copilot.

If omitted, returns both owned and shared meetings (equivalent to combining `me` and `shared`).

get.description:
Retrieve the full transcript for a specific meeting by its summary ID. Returns the complete transcript with speaker identification and timestamps.

**Required Feature:** `mixmaxApi` (API access must be enabled for your workspace)

**Workspace Access:** If "Allow workspace-wide transcript access via API" is enabled in Admin Settings > Meeting Copilot, users can access transcripts from all workspace members' meetings.

**Note:** The `id` parameter is the meeting summary ID (the `_id` field from the `/meetings/summaries/search` response).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The meeting summary ID. This is the `_id` field returned from the `/meetings/summaries/search` endpoint. URL encode the `_id` returned by that endpoint before appending it to this request url.

endTime.description: End time of period in which meetings of this type can be made. Format must match "HH:mm:ss".

enabled.description: Whether to allow meetings of this type to be booked on this day.
Whether to allow meetings of this type to be booked on this day.

defaults.description: Defaults to be used in the calendar invitation of meetings booked of this type.

buffer.description: The amount of time in between meetings, must be in the range of 0 - 60.

calendarIds.description: The Google Calendar IDs of the calendars on which meetings of this meeting type will be scheduled. If multiple calendars are added to a meeting type, meetings will be booked round-robin between those calendars.

Calendars at the beginning of this queue will be preferred for booking when someone selects an available timeslot for this meeting type where multiple calendars have availability.

get.description: Retrieves the recipients belonging to the specified sequence. The list of recipients only includes recipients that were activated, it does not include recipients currently in the draft area.  **Note**: This endpoint uses different pagination than most API endpoints. Rather than receiving an object with "results" and "next" keys, you will receive a single array of results as a response. Use the `offset` query parameter to fetch the next page of results. For example, if you used `limit=50` to retrieve the first page, then use `offset=50` to retrieve the second page, `offset=100` to retrieve the third page, and so on. You're limited to 10,000 total records. So if you're requesting with a `offset=9999`, you can only request `limit=1`.

CallRecordingInfo.description: Recording metadata. There is deliberately no media URL here — recordings are private, so audio is served only through `GET /calls/{id}/recording`.

RecordingSid.description: Identifier of the recording with the telephony provider.

RecordingDuration.description: Recording length in seconds, as reported by the telephony provider.

RecordingStartTime.description: When the recording started, as reported by the telephony provider.

CallSalesforceWho.description: The Salesforce contact or lead the call was logged against, hydrated when the call is linked to a CRM record. Present only for CRM-logged calls — treat every field as optional.

Id.description: Salesforce record Id of the contact or lead.

Name.description: Display name of the contact or lead.

normalizedEmail.description: Email address of the contact or lead.

Call.description: A call placed with the Mixmax Dialer. Only calls that were actually dialed appear in the API. Fields other than `_id`, `userId` and `created` may be absent depending on how the call ended and what it was logged against.

userId.description: The Mixmax user who placed the call.

user.description: The name and email of the Mixmax user who placed the call (the user in `userId`), so you can attribute calls without a separate lookup. They are looked up when you make the request, so they show the user's current profile, not their profile at the time of the call. Included on every call unless `fields` leaves it out. `null` when Mixmax has no user with that `userId`, which means their account was deleted; Mixmax deletes a deleted account's calls shortly afterwards.

name.description: The user's full name, or `null` if their profile has no name.

email.description: The user's email address as stored (compare it case-insensitively), or `null` if their profile has none.

created.description: When the call record was created, in epoch milliseconds. Results are ordered on this field, newest first.

completedAt.description: When the call ended. Absent while a call is in progress.

failedReason.description: Why the call failed, when `status` is `failed`.

phoneNumber.description: The number that was called, in E.164 format.

phoneNumberFormatted.description: The number that was called, formatted for display.

fromPhoneNumber.description: The Mixmax number the call was placed from.

countryCode.description: ISO country code of the number.

fromPhoneNumberType.description: Whether the call was placed from the user's own Mixmax number (`user`) or a local-presence number (`local`).

recordingEnabled.description: Whether recording was enabled for this call.

metadata.description: Linkage to CRM records and Mixmax tasks.

salesforce.description: Salesforce task linkage, present when the call was logged to Salesforce.

WhoId.description: Salesforce Id of the contact or lead the call was logged against.

WhatId.description: Salesforce Id of the related account or opportunity.

Subject.description: Subject of the logged Salesforce task.

Status.description: Status of the logged Salesforce task.

mixmaxTaskId.description: The Mixmax Call Task this call was placed from. Absent for ad-hoc calls.

fullName.description: Inline copy of the called contact's name. Often set on calls where the hydrated `metadata.salesforce.who` is absent.

comments.description: Notes the rep entered for the call.

results.description: The page of calls, newest first.

next.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass as the `next` query parameter. Treat cursors as opaque strings; their format is internal and may change.

previous.description: Opaque cursor for the previous page. Pass as the `previous` query parameter.

TaskSequence.description: Sequence context when the task was created by a sequence.

id.description: Identifier of the sequence that created the task.

name.description: Display name of the sequence.

stage.description: Identifier of the sequence stage that created the task.

Task.description: A Mixmax task visible to the API key owner. The available fields vary by task type.

assignee.description: The task assignee as either a Mixmax user ID or a decorated user object.

total.description: Total number of tasks matching the requested filters.

next.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when no next page exists.

previous.description: Opaque cursor for the previous page, or null when no previous page exists.
